name: CH32V005D6U6
title: CH32V006/CH32V005: 48 MHz QingKe RISC-V (RV32EmC) microcontrollers, 2.0 V to 5.5 V, 12-bit 3 Msps ADC, OPA, QFN12 to QFN32
summary: A family of small general-purpose RISC-V microcontrollers that run straight from a 2.0 V to 5.5 V supply at up to 48 MHz. CH32V005 carries 32 KB flash and 6 KB SRAM; CH32V006 up to 62 KB and 8 KB, plus touch-key sensing and a third timer. Both have a 12-bit ADC at up to 3 Msps, an op-amp that doubles as PGA or comparator, a 7-channel DMA, an advanced and a general 16-bit timer, two USARTs, I2C and (except the 12-pin parts) SPI. CH32V005D6U6 is the 12-pin 2 mm × 2 mm QFN member with 11 GPIOs, rated -40 °C to 85 °C.
key_figures: QingKe V2C RISC-V, RV32EmC, 48 MHz max
up to 62 KB code flash, 8 KB SRAM
2.0 V to 5.5 V (2.4 V min with ADC)
2.8 mA typ at 48 MHz on HSI, peripherals off
17.5 µA typ CH32V005, 10.2 µA typ CH32V006 at 3.3 V
12 MHz GBW, 64 MHz in high-speed mode; PGA ×4 to ×32

notes: Parts ending in 7 differ from those ending in 6 only in their wider temperature range.
ADC is external + internal channels; ADTM is the advanced timer, GPTM the general-purpose timer.

tables.title: Pin numbers and default functions
notes: Pin type: I is a TTL/CMOS Schmitt input, O a CMOS tri-state output, A an analog input or output, P a supply pin.
Pin 0 is the exposed pad of a QFN package.

On QSOP24 parts PA1 and PA6 share pin 17 inside the package; neither may be set as an output. On CH32V006F8U7, CH32V006F8P7, CH32V006D8U7, CH32V005F6U6, CH32V005F6P6 and CH32V005D6U6, PD7 and PA4 share one pin inside the package; the two must not both be outputs.
The reset pin is PA7 on CH32V006K8U7, PC5 on CH32V006E8R6/E8R7 and CH32V005E6R6, and PD7 on every other part.

CH32V006F4U6 has no OPA: on it the OPA functions are absent, PD7 lists TIM2_CH4/RST, PD1 lists TIM1_CH3N/SWIO/ADC_IETR, PD3 lists ADC_IN4/TIM2_CH2/USART1_CTS/ADC_RETR, PC5 lists TIM1_ETR/SPI_SCK, and PD0, PC2, PC4 and PD7 are typed I/O.
A function only works on a part that has the peripheral; the part-number table lists them.

circuits.title: Supply decoupling
circuits.description: The single supply rail feeds VDD with one 0.1 µF capacitor across VDD and VSS.

circuits.title: Analog supply and decoupling
circuits.description: The analog supply reference: 0.1 µF from VDD to VSS, with VSS on ground.

circuits.title: 24 MHz crystal on XI/XO
circuits.description: A 24 MHz crystal across XI (PA1) and XO (PA2) with a load capacitor from each pin to ground. The feedback resistor is inside the chip. The load capacitors are set by the crystal's specified load, normally with CL1 equal to CL2; 20 pF is the recommended load for a crystal of 60 Ω series resistance. PA1PA2_RM = 1 turns the two pins over to the oscillator.

parts.note: set by the crystal's load capacitance; equal to CL2
set by the crystal's load capacitance; equal to CL1

circuits.title: External clock into XI
circuits.description: An external square-wave clock of 3 MHz to 32 MHz drives XI (PA1) directly; XO (PA2) is left open. The input must reach 0.8 VDD high and 0.2 VDD low, with 40 % to 60 % duty cycle.

circuits.title: External reset button
circuits.description: A push button pulls the reset pin to ground. The pin carries an internal pull-up of about 45 kΩ and a pulse filter. An optional 0.1 µF capacitor from the pin to ground removes contact bounce. On the QFN12 parts the reset pin is PD7, which shares its pad with PA4.

circuits.title: ADC input connection
circuits.description: A signal source VAIN reaches an ADC input pin AINx through its source resistance RAIN; Cp, about 5 pF, is the stray capacitance of the pad and board on that input. Inside, the pin has clamp diodes to VDD and VSS and a sampling switch of RADC into the 4 pF hold capacitor. The largest RAIN for a given sampling time comes from the RAIN equation and tables; a larger Cp costs accuracy, which a lower fADC recovers. AINx is any ADC input; this circuit uses PA2 (ADC_IN0).

parts.note: stray capacitance of pad and board, about 5 pF

circuits.title: Supply current measurement
circuits.description: The supply current IDD is read by a current meter in series between the supply and VDD.

operation.text: CH32V006 and CH32V005 are one family on the QingKe V2C RISC-V core (RV32EmC). CH32V006 has up to 62 KB of code flash and 8 KB of SRAM, an 8-channel touch-key unit and the streamlined timer TIM3; CH32V005 has 32 KB of flash and 6 KB of SRAM, no touch keys and no TIM3. Model numbers ending in 6 run from -40 °C to 85 °C, those ending in 7 to 105 °C; otherwise the two are the same. CH32V006F4U6 is the cut-down member: 16 KB flash, 4 KB SRAM, one serial port, no OPA. The 12-pin parts have four external ADC channels and no SPI.

The core runs at up to 48 MHz with machine and user privilege levels, a two-level hardware interrupt stack and custom extension instructions; the m in EmC is the multiply subset of the M extension. The PFIC handles up to 255 vectors, of which 4 core interrupts and 25 peripheral interrupts are used now. It offers one NMI, hardware prologue and epilogue with no instruction cost, two vector-table-free fast slots, vectors as addresses or instructions, tail chaining and nesting two deep. The SysTick is a 32-bit up counter with reload (exception 15).

SRAM is up to 8 KB and is lost at power-down. Code flash (the user area) is up to 62 KB. The 3328-byte system flash holds the factory boot loader and can be joined to the user area with the WCH-LinkUtility tool. A 256-byte area holds the factory configuration words, which cannot be changed, and another 256 bytes holds the user option bytes. Flash is programmed and erased in 256-byte pages; a 1 KB sector can also be erased at once.

One supply, VDD = 2.0 V to 5.5 V, powers the I/O and the internal core regulator; with the ADC in use VDD must be at least 2.4 V, and above a 1 MHz sample rate at least 4.5 V. The I/O levels follow VDD. The regulator turns on after reset and has two modes: normal running, and a low-power mode used in Standby.

A power-on/power-down reset circuit is always on and holds the chip in reset while the supply is below VPOR/PDR, so no external reset parts are needed for start-up. The programmable voltage detector, enabled by software, compares VDD with one of four thresholds set by PLS[1:0] and can raise an interrupt as VDD falls through or rises through it. The reset pin, when used as reset, has its pull-up on and its pull-down off; it filters pulses shorter than 100 ns and passes pulses longer than 300 ns.

Sleep stops only the CPU clock; peripherals keep running and any interrupt or wake-up event resumes it, about 10 µs with the HSI. Standby combines SLEEPDEEP with peripheral clock gating: the HSI, HSE and PLL stop and the regulator drops to low power, while SRAM, registers and pin states are kept. It ends on any EXTI line (any of the 31 I/O lines or the auto-wake-up unit), an external reset on RST or an IWDG reset, and the chip resumes on the HSI in about 250 µs.

There are three sources: the factory-trimmed 24 MHz HSI RC, the 128 kHz LSI RC, and the HSE crystal or external-clock oscillator on XI/XO (PA1/PA2). The HSI or HSE may feed a ×2 PLL, and SYSCLK is taken from HSI, HSE or PLL, then divided by the HB prescaler (/1 to /256) to give HCLK, 48 MHz at most. The HSI is the clock after reset and after wake from Standby. The LSI clocks the IWDG and the auto-wake-up unit. MCO on PC4 can output HSI, HSE or PLLCLK. The ADC clock is HCLK divided by 2 to 128. With clock security on, a failed HSE used as system clock makes the chip fall back to the HSI and switches the HSE and PLL off, with an optional interrupt. The system clock monitor (SCM), when enabled, sends a brake signal to TIM1 and flags an interrupt if the system clock fails.

The DMA controller has seven channels that move data between memories and peripherals in any direction, with ring-buffer mode, per-channel request logic and programmable priority, length, source and destination. TIMx, ADC, USART, I2C and SPI can request it; DMA and CPU share the SRAM through an arbiter. The EXTI has 10 edge detectors, each set for rising, falling or both edges and individually masked, with a pending register; it catches pulses shorter than one HB clock (10 ns minimum width). Any of the 31 GPIOs can be routed to the external interrupt line.

The 12-bit ADC samples at up to 3 Msps with up to 8 external inputs and 2 internal ones, in single, continuous, scan or discontinuous mode with programmable sampling time per channel. Input range is VSS to VDD. IN8 reads the internal reference (1.2 V typ) and IN9 reads the OPA output directly. An analog watchdog watches selected channels and can reset the chip when a level leaves its window. The touch-key unit (CH32V006 only) measures up to 8 channels through the ADC inputs and leaves the key decision to a library or user code.

TIM1 is a 16-bit up/down advanced timer with a 16-bit prescaler, usable as a three-phase PWM generator over 6 channels with complementary outputs, dead-time insertion, repetition counter and brake input. TIM2 is a 16-bit up/down general timer with four channels for capture, compare, PWM and one-pulse output; using channels 3 and 4 gives channels 1 and 2 complementary outputs with dead time. TIM3 (CH32V006 only) is a 16-bit streamlined timer with four compare channels for internal signalling. Timers link to each other for synchronisation and freeze in debug. The IWDG is a 12-bit down counter on the LSI with 7 prescaler settings, runs in Standby and can be started by software or forced on by option byte. The WWDG is a 7-bit down counter on the main clock with an early-warning interrupt.

Two USARTs give full-duplex asynchronous and single-wire half-duplex links, LIN, IrDA SIR, CTS/RTS flow control, multiprocessor mode, a fractional baud generator and DMA. The SPI runs as master or slave up to 24 MHz, full or half duplex, multi-master, with 8- or 16-bit frames, programmable clock polarity and phase, hardware CRC and DMA, and supports SD/MMC basics. The I2C works as master or slave at standard and fast speed, with 7- or 10-bit addressing, dual 7-bit slave addresses and hardware CRC.

Up to 31 GPIOs on ports A (PA0-PA7), B (PB0-PB6), C (PC0-PC7) and D (PD0-PD7). Each pin is an input (floating, pull-up or pull-down), a push-pull or open-drain output, or a peripheral function, and every pin has switchable pull-up and pull-down resistors of about 45 kΩ. Pins can sink or source ±8 mA within the stated VOL/VOH and ±20 mA with relaxed levels. A lock mechanism freezes the configuration. When PA1PA2_RM = 1 the two pins belong to the oscillator. Where two port bits share one pin inside a package (PA1/PA6 on QSOP24, PD7/PA4 on the 20- and 12-pin parts except CH32V006F4U6), only one of them may be an output.

One OPA, usable as an amplifier, a PGA or a voltage comparator. Its inputs are chosen from several pins (P0-P3, N0-N2), and on CH32V006 the positive input can poll three channels in turn. The PGA gain is 4, 8, 16 or 32. The output goes to OPA_OUT0 (PD4) or OPA_OUT1 (PA5), and internally to ADC channel IN9 for small-signal measurement. A high-speed mode raises bandwidth from 12 MHz to 64 MHz and slew rate from 10 V/µs to 36 V/µs at 1.4 mA supply current. A VDD of at least 2.5 V is recommended for the OPA, and 2.7 V is the minimum in high-speed mode.

Debug runs over the serial debug interface: one-wire SDI on SWIO (PD1) by default, or two-wire SDI on SWDIO (PD1) and SWCLK (PB3) for faster download. The debug pins are active after power-up or reset and software may release them later. One-wire debug needs the HSI running. Each chip carries a unique ID.

Voltages refer to VSS. Minimum and maximum figures hold over the worst case of temperature, supply and clock; typical figures are at 25 °C with VDD = 3.3 V or 5 V. Figures from evaluation, simulation or process data are not tested in production; limits come from sample tests.

All package dimensions are in millimetres. Pin pitch is exact; every other dimension holds to ±0.2 mm or ±10 %, whichever is larger. The QFN exposed pad has a chamfered corner marking pin 1 and is ground.
